learn: A warm-up gets your body ready to move.
It makes your heart beat a little faster and warms your muscles.
Warm muscles are less likely to get hurt.
check: Gets your body ready to move
lessons.try: Do a warm-up: march in place, arm circles and gentle jumping for one minute.

learn: Check that your space is clear before you move.
Use equipment the right way, like rolling a ball, not throwing it at faces.
Wear shoes that fit and are tied.
check: Using equipment the right way keeps us...
lessons.try: Check your play area and move anything you could trip on.

learn: After exercise, we cool down to let our heart slow.
Walk slowly and take deep breaths.
Gentle stretches help muscles relax.
lessons.try: After playing, walk slowly and stretch your arms up high.

learn: Locomotor skills move you from one place to another.
Walking, running, hopping, skipping, galloping, sliding and leaping are locomotor skills.
A leap is a long step from one foot to the other.
check: Move you from place to place
A long step from one foot to the other
lessons.try: Do each locomotor skill across the room.

learn: A pathway is the path your body travels.
You can move in straight, curved or zigzag pathways.
Change pathways to avoid others.
lessons.try: Walk a straight path, then a curved path, then a zigzag path.

learn: You can move fast or slow.
You can move at a high level (on tiptoes), medium level or low level (crawling).
Combining speed and level makes movement interesting.
lessons.try: Move slowly at a low level, then fast at a high level.

learn: You can jump from two feet or one foot.
Bend your knees and swing your arms to jump higher or farther.
Push off with your toes.
check: Can you jump from one foot?
lessons.try: Try a two-foot jump, swinging your arms.

learn: Land on the balls of your feet with knees bent.
Bending your knees absorbs the landing, like a spring.
Keep your arms out for balance.
check: Bending your knees is like a...
lessons.try: Jump and freeze in a soft landing like a statue.

learn: Jumping rope builds a strong heart and legs.
Turn the rope with your wrists, not your whole arms.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope.
check: You turn the rope with your...
Just high enough to clear the rope
lessons.try: Jump over a rope on the ground ten times, then try a turning rope.

learn: For an overhand throw, stand sideways to your target.
Bring your arm back, step with the opposite foot and throw.
Follow through by letting your arm swing down across your body.
check: How should you stand for an overhand throw?
Letting your arm keep moving after the throw
lessons.try: Throw a soft ball overhand at a target on a wall.

learn: For a high ball, thumbs together, fingers up.
For a low ball, pinkies together, fingers down.
Bring the ball in to your body to soften the catch.
check: Bringing the ball to your body...
lessons.try: Have a partner toss high and low balls to you.

learn: Partners throw and catch together.
Say your partner's name before you throw so they are ready.
Move farther apart when you can catch ten in a row.
check: What should you do before you throw?
When should you move farther apart?
After ten catches in a row
lessons.try: Count how many catches in a row you and a partner can make.

learn: Step beside the ball with your non-kicking foot.
Kick with the inside or top of your foot, not your toes.
Keep your eyes on the ball.
check: Where does your non-kicking foot go?
Inside or top of your foot
lessons.try: Kick a ball to a target, like between two cones.

learn: Dribbling means moving the ball with small taps.
Keep the ball close so you can control it.
Use both feet.
check: Moving the ball with small taps
lessons.try: Dribble a ball around three cones and back.

learn: You can also dribble a ball with your hand, like in basketball.
Push the ball with your finger pads, not a slap.
Keep it at waist height and look up.
check: How high should the ball bounce?
lessons.try: Dribble a ball with one hand ten times, then switch.

learn: Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist.
It pumps blood all day and all night.
Exercise makes your heart stronger.
check: About the size of your fist
lessons.try: Make a fist. That is about the size of your heart.

learn: Activities that make you breathe hard are good for your heart.
Running, swimming, dancing and biking count.
Children should be active for at least 60 minutes every day.
check: How long should children be active each day?
Which is good for your heart?
Activities that make you breathe hard are good for your...
lessons.try: Dance for five minutes to fast music.

learn: Muscles help you move. They get stronger when you use them.
Climbing, jumping and carrying light things build strength.
Jumping also helps your bones grow strong.
lessons.try: Try five frog jumps and five bear crawls.

learn: Food is fuel for your body, like gas for a car.
Healthy food gives you energy to play and think.
Eating breakfast helps you get ready to learn.
lessons.try: Plan a healthy breakfast.

learn: Half your plate should be fruits and vegetables.
The other half should have grains and protein.
Add a serving of dairy, like milk or yogurt.
check: How much of your plate should be fruits and vegetables?
lessons.try: Draw a healthy plate for lunch.

learn: Your body needs water, especially when you exercise.
Water is the best drink when you are thirsty.
Drink before, during and after playing hard.
check: What is the best drink when thirsty?
When should you drink when playing hard?
lessons.try: Count how many cups of water you drink today.

learn: Washing hands removes germs that can make you sick.
Use soap and scrub for 20 seconds.
Wash before eating and after using the toilet.
lessons.try: Wash your hands while singing the alphabet song.

learn: Bathing or showering keeps your skin and hair clean.
Wear clean clothes and socks, especially after sweating.
Being clean helps you feel good and stay healthy.
lessons.try: Help sort your clothes into clean and dirty piles.

learn: Germs spread when we cough and sneeze.
Cough or sneeze into your elbow or a tissue.
Throw the tissue away and wash your hands.
check: Into your hand and touch things
What do you do with a used tissue?
lessons.try: Practise the elbow sneeze.

learn: Everyone has feelings: happy, sad, angry, scared, worried, excited.
Feelings can be big or small.
It is okay to have any feeling. What matters is what we do.
check: Is it okay to have any feeling?
What we do with our feelings
lessons.try: Tell a grown-up a feeling you had today and why.

learn: When a feeling is too big, you can calm your body.
Take five slow breaths, count to ten, or squeeze and relax your hands.
Asking for a break or talking to a grown-up also helps.
check: Can asking for a break help?
lessons.try: Practise five slow balloon breaths.

learn: Good friends share, take turns and use kind words.
Good friends include others: "Do you want to play?"
When you make a mistake, say sorry and make it right.
check: What can you say to include someone?
When you make a mistake, you...
Say sorry and make it right
lessons.try: Invite someone new to play a game.

learn: Wear a helmet when you ride a bike, scooter or skateboard.
Play in safe places that a grown-up has checked.
Never swim without a grown-up watching.
check: When should you wear a helmet?
Can you swim without a grown-up watching?
lessons.try: Check your helmet fits: snug, level and buckled.

learn: A stranger is someone you do not know.
Never go anywhere with a stranger, even if they offer a treat.
Online, never share your name, address or school, and tell a grown-up if anything makes you feel uncomfortable.
check: Should you go somewhere with a stranger who offers a treat?
What should you never share online?
If something online feels uncomfortable, you...
lessons.try: Practise saying "No!" and walking away to a trusted grown-up.

learn: An emergency is when someone is badly hurt, there is a fire or someone is in danger.
Call 911 or get a grown-up right away.
In a fire, get out, stay out and go to your family's meeting place. Stop, drop and roll if clothes catch fire.
check: What number do you call in an emergency?
If your clothes catch fire, you...
lessons.try: With your family, choose a meeting place outside your home.
